summary:
[  edit  ]
The  Vertex   SOP  allows you to edit/create attributes on a per-vertex (rather than per-point) basis. It is similar to the  Point SOP  in this respect. It supports two inputs, and will inherit the first input source by default.  If the second input have less primitives than the first input, it will cycle through the primitives and match the vertices.  If the primitive in the first input has more vertices than the matching primitive in the second input, the extra vertices are ignored.
There are currently three vertex attributes supported:
Diffuse Color
Alpha
Texture Coordinates
When the attribute is defined, it can only occur on either points or vertices, but not both. Thus, if the input geometry has a point attribute for diffuse color, the attribute will automatically be "elevated" to be a vertex attribute (if diffuse colors are added in the  Vertex   SOP ).
The  SOP  processes every vertex of every primitive. For each vertex processed, there are variables which allow you to know the:
Vertex  number of the primitive being processed
The number of vertices in the primitive being processed
The point which is referenced by the vertex
The primitive which contains the vertex
The total number of points
The total number of primitives
There are also local variables to find out the values of some point attributes (i.e. position, normal - if they exist), in addition to vertex attributes.  To access the attributes of the second input source, append a 2 to the variable.

parameters.label: Group
parameters.name: group
parameters.description: If there are input groups, specifying a group name in this field will cause this   SOP   to act only upon the group specified. Accepts patterns, as described in  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Color
parameters.name: doclr
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select between keeping the color, adding new color, or using no color for vertex color attributes from incoming geometry.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.name: diff
parameters.description: ⊞  - If you select 'Add Color' from the menu above, Cd color vertex attributes will be added/modified in the  SOP . Enter expressions below to control the values of the point colors. The attributes to modify are:  me.inputColor[0]  for red,  me.inputColor[1]  for green,  me.inputColor[2]  for blue, and  me.inputColor[3]  for alpha. If you select 'No Color' from the menu above, the Cd color vertex attribute will be removed from the  SOP .

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Control the alpha attribute in the same manner as the rgb colors above. Alpha is Cd[3] and comes from input via  me.inputColor[3]

parameters.label: Texture
parameters.name: douvw
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select between keeping the texture coordinates, adding new texture coordinates, or using no texture coordinates for the vertex texture attributes from incoming geometry.

parameters.label: Texture
parameters.name: map
parameters.description: ⊞  - If you select 'Add Texture' from the menu above, uv texture coordinate vertex attributes will be added/modified in the  SOP . Enter expressions here to control the values of the vertex texture coordinates here. The attributes to modify are:  me.inputTexture[0] ,  me.inputTexture[1]  and  me.inputTexture[2] . If you select 'No Texture' from the menu above, the uv texture coordinates vertex attribute will be removed from the  SOP .

parameters.label: Crease
parameters.name: docrease
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select between keeping the crease, adding new crease, or using no crease for creaseweight attribute from incoming geometry.

parameters.label: The  Crease Weight  attribute can be used to set individual edge crease weights for sub
parameters.description: division surfaces (see  Subdivide SOP  ). This vertex attribute defines the weight for the edge which goes from that vertex to the next vertex in the polygon. For example, with a triangle (which has vertices 0, 1, 2), the attribute for vertex 1 defines the crease weight for the edge (1, 2). The attribute for vertex 2 defines the crease weight for edge (2, 0). The crease weight should be greater than 0. The larger the value for crease weights, the sharper the edge will be when sub-divided.

parameters.label: Crease
parameters.name: crease
parameters.description: If you select 'Add Crease' from the menu above, enter expressions here to control the values of the creaseweights here. The attribute to modify is: me.inputVertex.creaseWeight[0]. Values for the weight of the vertex can range from 0.0001 to infinity.

parameters.label: You can have set of images in a  TOP , and apply all of them in one material to different parts of an object. This allows you to have a pre
parameters.description: rendered animation clip with the clip playing at different speeds and time offsets on different surfaces.

parameters.label: You can adjust the material frame time by the first vertex/point texture W component (texture coordinated are U (horizontal), V (vertical) and W (one of a set of texture images). A texture (W) value of
parameters.description: 1 moves back in time 1 frame. This lets you apply different frames to many polygons simultaneously using the  Vertex   SOP , or  Point SOP .

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: The Graphics Processing Unit. This is the high
parameters.description: speed, many-core processor of the graphics card/chip that takes geometry, images and data from the CPU and creates images and processed data.

Attribute Convert POP * **¿Qué hace?** Permite **copiar un atributo de un tipo de geometría a otro**.
